globals THREAD MODULE [FIRST COUNT] | info globals THREAD MODULE [FIRST COUNT]

ni [THREAD] | nexti [THREAD] (current genuine native trap/top frame; qualified instructions, same-owner direct branches and typed Wasm calls)
ni proves owned targets or a typed-call continuation before execution; VM/unknown targets and unsupported returns retain the stop. First establish step asm THREAD.
disassemble THREAD STOP_ID COUNT (1..32 instructions; no address or offset input)
disassemble-range THREAD STOP_ID COUNT BYTE_OFFSET INSTRUCTION_OFFSET SYMBOLS (bounded owner; COUNT 1..32, SYMBOLS 0|1)
memory MODULE MEMORY OFFSET LENGTH | replace MODULE FUNCTION GENERATION BODY_FILE | help | quit
catch wasm EVENT MODULE FUNCTION|all | info wasm-events | delete|enable|disable wasm-event ID
trace wasm on [EVENT] | trace wasm off|clear | trace wasm read [AFTER_SEQUENCE [COUNT]] (COUNT=1..128)
wasm-script COMMAND; COMMAND (up to 16 diagnostic/policy commands, including ABI-checked replace; no resume/step or host evaluation)
info registers [REGISTER] | info registers THREAD STOP_ID [REGISTER] (real native trap, top frame only)
ptype NAME | ptype THREAD STOP_ID NAME (scoped C/C++/Rust type layout)
print EXPR | print THREAD STOP_ID EXPR (bounded copied guest selectors, integer/f32/f64 arithmetic, builtin numeric casts and sizeof; no calls)
print-frame THREAD STOP_ID FRAME EXPR | ptype-frame THREAD STOP_ID FRAME EXPR (explicit source frame, any expression prefix)
Rust tuple fields: pair.0 / pair.1; Zig conventional pointer dereference: p.* / p.*.field (owned guest bytes only).
display EXPR | info display | undisplay [ID] | enable|disable|delete display [ID]
Displays: at most32 printable expressions of256 bytes; evaluate source frame0 at each new genuine sole-thread stop. Unavailable values retain the entry; no saved pointer/value is reused.
Wasm EVENT: all|throw|exception|gc|memory|table|atomic|call|reference|simd|control. Events are BEFORE instructions, not committed effects.
Trace holds the newest 512 observations, reports overwritten entries, and never invokes scripts on a guest thread.
wait observes a stop/guest exit for at most two seconds; Ctrl+C separately requests a cooperative pause.
IDs and byte offsets are decimal; offsets are relative to the function expression and must name an emitted safe point.
break-source compares embedded DWARF or source-map paths exactly and opens no source text file.
locals source shows only current cooperative numeric direct-local/constant values; unsupported locations are unavailable.
frames [THREAD STOP_ID [FIRST COUNT]], frame [N|THREAD STOP_ID N], up/down [COUNT|THREAD STOP_ID COUNT] select real source frames.
frames wasm THREAD STOP_ID FIRST COUNT lists canonical Wasm frames without DWARF; pages contain at most128 rows and report the full total.
Caller values require their authenticated saved source PC and typed packet; unavailable locations are reported; resume/replacement/native stepping retire selection.
print/ptype THREAD STOP_ID FRAME NAME and locals source THREAD STOP_ID FRAME query a frame atomically without changing selection.
step wasm (also step THREAD or s THREAD) resumes all participants and stops at the next emitted
Wasm instruction safe point; other participants may advance before parking.
Wasm over skips child/tail-successor activations; out follows this activation through tail calls to its caller or guest exit.
Both use actual Wasm activation identities without DWARF; breakpoints and catchpoints interrupt over/out.
source into/over execute the innermost activation; out follows a selected DWARF frame or the current physical source-map frame. Actual full-JIT activation identities and DWARF scopes or Source Map v3 coordinates are required.
asm executes exactly one native instruction on a qualified LLVM-full JIT thread; other guests stay stopped.
memory reads at most 256 bytes and requires all guest threads stopped.
locals shows up to 256 typed values from the selected stopped thread.
replacement requires an owner-controlled regular body file, exact function ABI, and a stopped guest without an active target frame.
Use tools/debug/secure_server.py for an authorized server launched before guest entry.
Interactive c/continue waits for an actual stop; c&/continue& runs in the background.
Piped/script input keeps asynchronous continue; controller/server/DAP resume is unchanged.
Ctrl+C cancels partial input and requests a cooperative pause; a blocked host timeout keeps its request pending.
Up/Down or Ctrl+P/Ctrl+N recall 32 commands; Ctrl+A/E/B/F, Backspace, Ctrl+U/K/W edit the line.
Ctrl+_ or Ctrl+X Ctrl+U undo current input edits; Alt+F/B move by word and Alt+D/Alt+Backspace kill words.
Ctrl+Y restores killed input text; the command still needs Enter and stays within 8448 input bytes (WASIp1 text4096, legacy grammar512, raw memory256 bytes).
Ctrl+T transposes characters; Ctrl+V quotes printable input (newline/tab become spaces); Ctrl+O accepts and recalls the next history line.
Ctrl/Alt+Left/Right move by word; Alt+< / Alt+> select first history / current draft; Alt+digits repeat bounded input edits.
Bracketed paste treats newlines as spaces and requires Enter after its closing marker; overflow or incomplete markers reject the whole line.
Ctrl+L redraws; Tab completes commands, replace/tui source paths and current source variables/members and break MODULE function symbols; Ctrl+R/S search history backward/forward, Ctrl+G restores the search draft. Alt+Y cycles the immediate prior yank.
Empty Enter repeats eligible step/query commands; replacement/scripts/resume are never implicitly repeated.
s/step, n/next, finish select source into/over/out; si/stepi, bt/where, disas use the sole current stopped thread.
until/u FILE:LINE|LINE | advance/adv FILE:LINE|LINE (sole stopped thread, innermost frame); explicit until/advance THREAD STOP FILE:LINE|LINE.
Exact embedded statement in the origin module; until skips recursive calls, advance may enter them; both stop after return.
Explicit s THREAD/step THREAD retain Wasm stepping. i r, i b, i threads are info aliases.
Ctrl+D deletes under the cursor; on empty input it behaves as EOF.
Unique command prefixes (cont, hel, info reg) and GDB aliases (backtrace, f, d/del) are accepted; ambiguous prefixes are rejected.
LLDB aliases: thread step-in/step-over/step-out/step-inst/step-inst-over, thread backtrace/list, process continue/interrupt/status, frame variable/select, register read, breakpoint list/set/delete.
Breakpoints use explicit Wasm identities: b MODULE FUNCTION OFFSET or b MODULE FILE:LINE; unique published function symbols are supported; arbitrary native addresses and VM/host debugging remain unavailable.
Managed CLI quit requests bounded real cleanup; pending keeps owners and permits status/help/quit retry.
quit force explicitly terminates this process without claiming finalizers. CtrlD may retain a pending prompt.
A standalone launcher may preselect process termination after actual pipe EOF cannot complete cleanup.
Without an installed managed cleanup owner, quit/EOF retains the launcher's process termination policy.

Conditions evaluate at a genuine complete cooperative stop, frame0 of the actual hitting thread; false resumes, unavailable retains the stop.
continue | wait | pause | step wasm THREAD [into|over|out] | status | info threads | bt THREAD | locals THREAD
step source THREAD [into|over|out] | step asm THREAD | locals source THREAD
globals THREAD MODULE [FIRST COUNT] | info globals THREAD MODULE [FIRST COUNT]
table THREAD MODULE TABLE [FIRST COUNT] | info table THREAD MODULE TABLE [FIRST COUNT]
operands THREAD [FRAME [FIRST COUNT]] | info operands THREAD [FRAME [FIRST COUNT]]
locals wasm THREAD [FRAME [FIRST COUNT]] (COUNT 1..64; actual typed stop, no host addresses)
saved THREAD [FRAME [FIRST COUNT]] | controls THREAD [FRAME [FIRST COUNT]] | handlers THREAD [FRAME [FIRST COUNT]]

unset wasip1 fd MODULE FD OLD_BASE OLD_INHERIT

set wasip1 import-group HEXPATH MODULE[:RESOURCE=FD,...]... [if-stop N]

set wasm global MODULE GLOBAL THREAD bits i32|i64|f32|f64|v128 HEX [HEX]

WASIp1 text uses hex bytes (- means empty), up to 4096 raw bytes; rights accept decimal or 0x hex and may only decrease.
ni [THREAD] | nexti [THREAD] (current genuine native trap/top frame; qualified instructions, same-owner direct branches and typed Wasm calls)
ni proves owned targets or a typed-call continuation before execution; VM/unknown targets and unsupported returns retain the stop. First establish step asm THREAD.
disassemble THREAD STOP_ID COUNT (1..32 instructions; no address or offset input)
disassemble-range THREAD STOP_ID COUNT BYTE_OFFSET INSTRUCTION_OFFSET SYMBOLS (bounded owner; COUNT 1..32, SYMBOLS 0|1)
memory MODULE MEMORY OFFSET LENGTH | replace MODULE FUNCTION GENERATION BODY_FILE | help | quit
catch wasm EVENT MODULE FUNCTION|all | info wasm-events | delete|enable|disable wasm-event ID
trace wasm on [EVENT] | trace wasm off|clear | trace wasm read [AFTER_SEQUENCE [COUNT]] (COUNT=1..128)
wasm-script COMMAND; COMMAND (up to 16 diagnostic/policy commands, including ABI-checked replace; no resume/step or host evaluation)
info registers [REGISTER] | info registers THREAD STOP_ID [REGISTER] (real native trap, top frame only)
ptype NAME | ptype THREAD STOP_ID NAME (scoped C/C++/Rust type layout)
print EXPR | print THREAD STOP_ID EXPR (bounded copied guest selectors, integer/f32/f64 arithmetic, builtin numeric casts and sizeof; no calls)
print-frame THREAD STOP_ID FRAME EXPR | ptype-frame THREAD STOP_ID FRAME EXPR (explicit source frame, any expression prefix)
Rust tuple fields: pair.0 / pair.1; Zig conventional pointer dereference: p.* / p.*.field (owned guest bytes only).
display EXPR | info display | undisplay [ID] | enable|disable|delete display [ID]
Displays: at most32 printable expressions of256 bytes; evaluate source frame0 at each new genuine sole-thread stop. Unavailable values retain the entry; no saved pointer/value is reused.
Wasm EVENT: all|throw|exception|gc|memory|table|atomic|call|reference|simd|control. Events are BEFORE instructions, not committed effects.
Trace holds the newest 512 observations, reports overwritten entries, and never invokes scripts on a guest thread.
wait observes a stop/guest exit for at most two seconds; Ctrl+C separately requests a cooperative pause.
IDs and byte offsets are decimal; offsets are relative to the function expression and must name an emitted safe point.
break-source compares embedded DWARF or source-map paths exactly and opens no source text file.
locals source shows only current cooperative numeric direct-local/constant values; unsupported locations are unavailable.
frames [THREAD STOP_ID [FIRST COUNT]], frame [N|THREAD STOP_ID N], up/down [COUNT|THREAD STOP_ID COUNT] select real source frames.
frames wasm THREAD STOP_ID FIRST COUNT lists canonical Wasm frames without DWARF; pages contain at most128 rows and report the full total.
Caller values require their authenticated saved source PC and typed packet; unavailable locations are reported; resume/replacement/native stepping retire selection.
print/ptype THREAD STOP_ID FRAME NAME and locals source THREAD STOP_ID FRAME query a frame atomically without changing selection.
step wasm (also step THREAD or s THREAD) resumes all participants and stops at the next emitted
Wasm instruction safe point; other participants may advance before parking.
Wasm over skips child/tail-successor activations; out follows this activation through tail calls to its caller or guest exit.
Both use actual Wasm activation identities without DWARF; breakpoints and catchpoints interrupt over/out.
source into/over execute the innermost activation; out follows a selected DWARF frame or the current physical source-map frame. Actual full-JIT activation identities and DWARF scopes or Source Map v3 coordinates are required.
asm executes exactly one native instruction on a qualified LLVM-full JIT thread; other guests stay stopped.
memory reads at most 256 bytes and requires all guest threads stopped.
locals shows up to 256 typed values from the selected stopped thread.
replacement requires an owner-controlled regular body file, exact function ABI, and a stopped guest without an active target frame.
Use tools/debug/secure_server.py for an authorized server launched before guest entry.
Interactive c/continue waits for an actual stop; c&/continue& runs in the background.
Piped/script input keeps asynchronous continue; controller/server/DAP resume is unchanged.
Ctrl+C cancels partial input and requests a cooperative pause; a blocked host timeout keeps its request pending.
Up/Down or Ctrl+P/Ctrl+N recall 32 commands; Ctrl+A/E/B/F, Backspace, Ctrl+U/K/W edit the line.
Ctrl+_ or Ctrl+X Ctrl+U undo current input edits; Alt+F/B move by word and Alt+D/Alt+Backspace kill words.
Ctrl+Y restores killed input text; the command still needs Enter and stays within 8448 input bytes (WASIp1 text4096, legacy grammar512, raw memory256 bytes).
Ctrl+T transposes characters; Ctrl+V quotes printable input (newline/tab become spaces); Ctrl+O accepts and recalls the next history line.
Ctrl/Alt+Left/Right move by word; Alt+< / Alt+> select first history / current draft; Alt+digits repeat bounded input edits.
Bracketed paste treats newlines as spaces and requires Enter after its closing marker; overflow or incomplete markers reject the whole line.
Ctrl+L redraws; Tab completes commands, replace/tui source paths and current source variables/members and break MODULE function symbols; Ctrl+R/S search history backward/forward, Ctrl+G restores the search draft. Alt+Y cycles the immediate prior yank.
Empty Enter repeats eligible step/query commands; replacement/scripts/resume are never implicitly repeated.
s/step, n/next, finish select source into/over/out; si/stepi, bt/where, disas use the sole current stopped thread.
until/u FILE:LINE|LINE | advance/adv FILE:LINE|LINE (sole stopped thread, innermost frame); explicit until/advance THREAD STOP FILE:LINE|LINE.
Exact embedded statement in the origin module; until skips recursive calls, advance may enter them; both stop after return.
Explicit s THREAD/step THREAD retain Wasm stepping. i r, i b, i threads are info aliases.
Ctrl+D deletes under the cursor; on empty input it behaves as EOF.
Unique command prefixes (cont, hel, info reg) and GDB aliases (backtrace, f, d/del) are accepted; ambiguous prefixes are rejected.
LLDB aliases: thread step-in/step-over/step-out/step-inst/step-inst-over, thread backtrace/list, process continue/interrupt/status, frame variable/select, register read, breakpoint list/set/delete.
Breakpoints use explicit Wasm identities: b MODULE FUNCTION OFFSET or b MODULE FILE:LINE; unique published function symbols are supported; arbitrary native addresses and VM/host debugging remain unavailable.
Managed CLI quit requests bounded real cleanup; pending keeps owners and permits status/help/quit retry.
quit force explicitly terminates this process without claiming finalizers. CtrlD may retain a pending prompt.
A standalone launcher may preselect process termination after actual pipe EOF cannot complete cleanup.
Without an installed managed cleanup owner, quit/EOF retains the launcher's process termination policy.

tui enable|disable | tui source PATH | layout src|asm|split|regs|wasm|wasip1|next | focus next|prev|cmd|code
Ctrl+X A toggles TUI; Ctrl+X 1/2 selects source/split; PgUp/PgDn scrolls the focused pane; Ctrl+L refreshes/resizes.
TUI uses current authenticated replies; asm/register views never open VM/runtime code. Source text is bounded local file data.
break MODULE SYMBOL | b MODULE SYMBOL (exact unambiguous live DWARF function; Tab completes names)
break MODULE FUNCTION BYTE_OFFSET | break-source MODULE FILE:LINE | delete BREAKPOINT | enable [BREAKPOINT] | disable [BREAKPOINT] | ignore BREAKPOINT COUNT | info breakpoints
break/break-source ... ignore COUNT installs the initial hit policy atomically; no unconditional registration window.
break/break-source ... [ignore COUNT] if EXPR | condition BREAKPOINT [EXPR] (bounded read-only source condition; omitted EXPR clears)
Conditions evaluate at a genuine complete cooperative stop, frame0 of the actual hitting thread; false resumes, unavailable retains the stop.
continue | wait | pause | step wasm THREAD [into|over|out] | status | info threads | bt THREAD | locals THREAD
step source THREAD [into|over|out] | step asm THREAD | locals source THREAD
globals THREAD MODULE [FIRST COUNT] | info globals THREAD MODULE [FIRST COUNT]
table THREAD MODULE TABLE [FIRST COUNT] | info table THREAD MODULE TABLE [FIRST COUNT]
operands THREAD [FRAME [FIRST COUNT]] | info operands THREAD [FRAME [FIRST COUNT]]
locals wasm THREAD [FRAME [FIRST COUNT]] (COUNT 1..64; actual typed stop, no host addresses)
saved THREAD [FRAME [FIRST COUNT]] | controls THREAD [FRAME [FIRST COUNT]] | handlers THREAD [FRAME [FIRST COUNT]]
control-params|control-results|handler-params THREAD FRAME CONTROL_OR_CLAUSE [FIRST COUNT]
  Controls and handlers are lexical Wasm layouts; saved values use actual if parameters, not native catch state.
members locals|operands|saved|globals|table THREAD MODULE FRAME TABLE ROOT FIRST COUNT [PATH...]
path create locals|operands|saved|globals|table THREAD MODULE FRAME TABLE ROOT [PATH...]
path extend SESSION HANDLE [PATH...] (returns new handle; retires parent)
path members SESSION HANDLE FIRST COUNT | path clear
  FRAME/TABLE zero where unused; ROOT/PATH are original indices, at most 16 edges and 64 members.
info wasip1 args|env|fds|preopens MODULE [FIRST COUNT]
trace wasip1 on [NAME|all] | off | clear | read [AFTER COUNT]
set wasip1 file MODULE HEXBYTES | set wasip1 fd-dup MODULE FD OLD_BASE OLD_INHERIT
unset wasip1 fd MODULE FD OLD_BASE OLD_INHERIT
set wasip1 checkpoint MODULE SLOT | set wasip1 restore MODULE SLOT bindings|strict
unset wasip1 checkpoint MODULE SLOT (SLOT 0..7; live environment only)
set wasip1 export MODULE HEXPATH | set wasip1 import MODULE HEXPATH [RESOURCE=TARGET_FD,...]
set wasip1 export-group HEXPATH MODULE... [if-stop N]
set wasip1 import-group HEXPATH MODULE[:RESOURCE=FD,...]... [if-stop N]
portable WASIp1: content external; configure target mnt with matching guest names; pair with Wasm checkpoint
Checkpoint Wasm and WASIp1 together at the same cooperative stop. External IO is not rolled back.
set wasm memory MODULE MEMORY THREAD OFFSET bytes HEX (1..256 bytes; guest address order)
set wasm global MODULE GLOBAL THREAD bits i32|i64|f32|f64|v128 HEX [HEX]
set wasm global MODULE GLOBAL THREAD null|i31 VALUE|function MODULE FUNCTION
set wasm table MODULE TABLE ELEMENT THREAD null|i31 VALUE|function MODULE FUNCTION

set wasm global|table ... from globals MODULE INDEX | from table MODULE TABLE ELEMENT
set wasm global|table ... from handle SESSION HANDLE [path EDGES...]
set wasm member THREAD locals|operands|saved FRAME INDEX [path EDGES...] at MEMBER SOURCE
set wasm member THREAD globals MODULE INDEX | table MODULE TABLE ELEMENT [path EDGES...] at MEMBER SOURCE
set wasm member THREAD handle SESSION HANDLE [path EDGES...] at MEMBER SOURCE

set wasip1 env MODULE HEXKEY HEXVALUE

unset wasip1 env MODULE HEXKEY | set wasip1 rights MODULE FD OLD_BASE OLD_INHERIT NEW_BASE NEW_INHERIT
WASIp1 text uses hex bytes (- means empty), up to 4096 raw bytes; rights accept decimal or 0x hex and may only decrease.
ni [THREAD] | nexti [THREAD] (current genuine native trap/top frame; qualified instructions, same-owner direct branches and typed Wasm calls)
ni proves owned targets or a typed-call continuation before execution; VM/unknown targets and unsupported returns retain the stop. First establish step asm THREAD.
disassemble THREAD STOP_ID COUNT (1..32 instructions; no address or offset input)
disassemble-range THREAD STOP_ID COUNT BYTE_OFFSET INSTRUCTION_OFFSET SYMBOLS (bounded owner; COUNT 1..32, SYMBOLS 0|1)
memory MODULE MEMORY OFFSET LENGTH | replace MODULE FUNCTION GENERATION BODY_FILE | help | quit
catch wasm EVENT MODULE FUNCTION|all | info wasm-events | delete|enable|disable wasm-event ID
trace wasm on [EVENT] | trace wasm off|clear | trace wasm read [AFTER_SEQUENCE [COUNT]] (COUNT=1..128)
wasm-script COMMAND; COMMAND (up to 16 diagnostic/policy commands, including ABI-checked replace; no resume/step or host evaluation)
info registers [REGISTER] | info registers THREAD STOP_ID [REGISTER] (real native trap, top frame only)
ptype NAME | ptype THREAD STOP_ID NAME (scoped C/C++/Rust type layout)
print EXPR | print THREAD STOP_ID EXPR (bounded copied guest selectors, integer/f32/f64 arithmetic, builtin numeric casts and sizeof; no calls)
print-frame THREAD STOP_ID FRAME EXPR | ptype-frame THREAD STOP_ID FRAME EXPR (explicit source frame, any expression prefix)
Rust tuple fields: pair.0 / pair.1; Zig conventional pointer dereference: p.* / p.*.field (owned guest bytes only).
display EXPR | info display | undisplay [ID] | enable|disable|delete display [ID]
Displays: at most32 printable expressions of256 bytes; evaluate source frame0 at each new genuine sole-thread stop. Unavailable values retain the entry; no saved pointer/value is reused.
Wasm EVENT: all|throw|exception|gc|memory|table|atomic|call|reference|simd|control. Events are BEFORE instructions, not committed effects.
Trace holds the newest 512 observations, reports overwritten entries, and never invokes scripts on a guest thread.
wait observes a stop/guest exit for at most two seconds; Ctrl+C separately requests a cooperative pause.
IDs and byte offsets are decimal; offsets are relative to the function expression and must name an emitted safe point.
break-source compares embedded DWARF or source-map paths exactly and opens no source text file.
locals source shows only current cooperative numeric direct-local/constant values; unsupported locations are unavailable.
frames [THREAD STOP_ID [FIRST COUNT]], frame [N|THREAD STOP_ID N], up/down [COUNT|THREAD STOP_ID COUNT] select real source frames.
frames wasm THREAD STOP_ID FIRST COUNT lists canonical Wasm frames without DWARF; pages contain at most128 rows and report the full total.
Caller values require their authenticated saved source PC and typed packet; unavailable locations are reported; resume/replacement/native stepping retire selection.
print/ptype THREAD STOP_ID FRAME NAME and locals source THREAD STOP_ID FRAME query a frame atomically without changing selection.
step wasm (also step THREAD or s THREAD) resumes all participants and stops at the next emitted
Wasm instruction safe point; other participants may advance before parking.
Wasm over skips child/tail-successor activations; out follows this activation through tail calls to its caller or guest exit.
Both use actual Wasm activation identities without DWARF; breakpoints and catchpoints interrupt over/out.
source into/over execute the innermost activation; out follows a selected DWARF frame or the current physical source-map frame. Actual full-JIT activation identities and DWARF scopes or Source Map v3 coordinates are required.
asm executes exactly one native instruction on a qualified LLVM-full JIT thread; other guests stay stopped.
memory reads at most 256 bytes and requires all guest threads stopped.
locals shows up to 256 typed values from the selected stopped thread.
replacement requires an owner-controlled regular body file, exact function ABI, and a stopped guest without an active target frame.
Use tools/debug/secure_server.py for an authorized server launched before guest entry.
Interactive c/continue waits for an actual stop; c&/continue& runs in the background.
Piped/script input keeps asynchronous continue; controller/server/DAP resume is unchanged.
Ctrl+C cancels partial input and requests a cooperative pause; a blocked host timeout keeps its request pending.
Up/Down or Ctrl+P/Ctrl+N recall 32 commands; Ctrl+A/E/B/F, Backspace, Ctrl+U/K/W edit the line.
Ctrl+_ or Ctrl+X Ctrl+U undo current input edits; Alt+F/B move by word and Alt+D/Alt+Backspace kill words.
Ctrl+Y restores killed input text; the command still needs Enter and stays within 8448 input bytes (WASIp1 text4096, legacy grammar512, raw memory256 bytes).
Ctrl+T transposes characters; Ctrl+V quotes printable input (newline/tab become spaces); Ctrl+O accepts and recalls the next history line.
Ctrl/Alt+Left/Right move by word; Alt+< / Alt+> select first history / current draft; Alt+digits repeat bounded input edits.
Bracketed paste treats newlines as spaces and requires Enter after its closing marker; overflow or incomplete markers reject the whole line.
Ctrl+L redraws; Tab completes commands, replace/tui source paths and current source variables/members and break MODULE function symbols; Ctrl+R/S search history backward/forward, Ctrl+G restores the search draft. Alt+Y cycles the immediate prior yank.
Empty Enter repeats eligible step/query commands; replacement/scripts/resume are never implicitly repeated.
s/step, n/next, finish select source into/over/out; si/stepi, bt/where, disas use the sole current stopped thread.
until/u FILE:LINE|LINE | advance/adv FILE:LINE|LINE (sole stopped thread, innermost frame); explicit until/advance THREAD STOP FILE:LINE|LINE.
Exact embedded statement in the origin module; until skips recursive calls, advance may enter them; both stop after return.
Explicit s THREAD/step THREAD retain Wasm stepping. i r, i b, i threads are info aliases.
Ctrl+D deletes under the cursor; on empty input it behaves as EOF.
Unique command prefixes (cont, hel, info reg) and GDB aliases (backtrace, f, d/del) are accepted; ambiguous prefixes are rejected.
LLDB aliases: thread step-in/step-over/step-out/step-inst/step-inst-over, thread backtrace/list, process continue/interrupt/status, frame variable/select, register read, breakpoint list/set/delete.
Breakpoints use explicit Wasm identities: b MODULE FUNCTION OFFSET or b MODULE FILE:LINE; unique published function symbols are supported; arbitrary native addresses and VM/host debugging remain unavailable.
Managed CLI quit requests bounded real cleanup; pending keeps owners and permits status/help/quit retry.
quit force explicitly terminates this process without claiming finalizers. CtrlD may retain a pending prompt.
A standalone launcher may preselect process termination after actual pipe EOF cannot complete cleanup.
Without an installed managed cleanup owner, quit/EOF retains the launcher's process termination policy.

tui enable|disable | tui source PATH | layout src|asm|split|regs|wasm|wasip1|next | focus next|prev|cmd|code
Ctrl+X A toggles TUI; Ctrl+X 1/2 selects source/split; PgUp/PgDn scrolls the focused pane; Ctrl+L refreshes/resizes.
TUI uses current authenticated replies; asm/register views never open VM/runtime code. Source text is bounded local file data.
break MODULE SYMBOL | b MODULE SYMBOL (exact unambiguous live DWARF function; Tab completes names)
break MODULE FUNCTION BYTE_OFFSET | break-source MODULE FILE:LINE | delete BREAKPOINT | enable [BREAKPOINT] | disable [BREAKPOINT] | ignore BREAKPOINT COUNT | info breakpoints
break/break-source ... ignore COUNT installs the initial hit policy atomically; no unconditional registration window.
break/break-source ... [ignore COUNT] if EXPR | condition BREAKPOINT [EXPR] (bounded read-only source condition; omitted EXPR clears)
Conditions evaluate at a genuine complete cooperative stop, frame0 of the actual hitting thread; false resumes, unavailable retains the stop.
continue | wait | pause | step wasm THREAD [into|over|out] | status | info threads | bt THREAD | locals THREAD
step source THREAD [into|over|out] | step asm THREAD | locals source THREAD
globals THREAD MODULE [FIRST COUNT] | info globals THREAD MODULE [FIRST COUNT]
table THREAD MODULE TABLE [FIRST COUNT] | info table THREAD MODULE TABLE [FIRST COUNT]
operands THREAD [FRAME [FIRST COUNT]] | info operands THREAD [FRAME [FIRST COUNT]]
locals wasm THREAD [FRAME [FIRST COUNT]] (COUNT 1..64; actual typed stop, no host addresses)
saved THREAD [FRAME [FIRST COUNT]] | controls THREAD [FRAME [FIRST COUNT]] | handlers THREAD [FRAME [FIRST COUNT]]
control-params|control-results|handler-params THREAD FRAME CONTROL_OR_CLAUSE [FIRST COUNT]
  Controls and handlers are lexical Wasm layouts; saved values use actual if parameters, not native catch state.
members locals|operands|saved|globals|table THREAD MODULE FRAME TABLE ROOT FIRST COUNT [PATH...]
path create locals|operands|saved|globals|table THREAD MODULE FRAME TABLE ROOT [PATH...]
path extend SESSION HANDLE [PATH...] (returns new handle; retires parent)
path members SESSION HANDLE FIRST COUNT | path clear
  FRAME/TABLE zero where unused; ROOT/PATH are original indices, at most 16 edges and 64 members.
info wasip1 args|env|fds|preopens MODULE [FIRST COUNT]
trace wasip1 on [NAME|all] | off | clear | read [AFTER COUNT]
set wasip1 file MODULE HEXBYTES | set wasip1 fd-dup MODULE FD OLD_BASE OLD_INHERIT
unset wasip1 fd MODULE FD OLD_BASE OLD_INHERIT
set wasip1 checkpoint MODULE SLOT | set wasip1 restore MODULE SLOT bindings|strict
unset wasip1 checkpoint MODULE SLOT (SLOT 0..7; live environment only)
set wasip1 export MODULE HEXPATH | set wasip1 import MODULE HEXPATH [RESOURCE=TARGET_FD,...]
set wasip1 export-group HEXPATH MODULE... [if-stop N]
set wasip1 import-group HEXPATH MODULE[:RESOURCE=FD,...]... [if-stop N]
portable WASIp1: content external; configure target mnt with matching guest names; pair with Wasm checkpoint
Checkpoint Wasm and WASIp1 together at the same cooperative stop. External IO is not rolled back.
set wasm memory MODULE MEMORY THREAD OFFSET bytes HEX (1..256 bytes; guest address order)
set wasm global MODULE GLOBAL THREAD bits i32|i64|f32|f64|v128 HEX [HEX]
set wasm global MODULE GLOBAL THREAD null|i31 VALUE|function MODULE FUNCTION
set wasm table MODULE TABLE ELEMENT THREAD null|i31 VALUE|function MODULE FUNCTION
set wasm global|table ... from locals|operands|saved FRAME INDEX [path EDGES...]
set wasm global|table ... from globals MODULE INDEX | from table MODULE TABLE ELEMENT
set wasm global|table ... from handle SESSION HANDLE [path EDGES...]
set wasm member THREAD locals|operands|saved FRAME INDEX [path EDGES...] at MEMBER SOURCE
set wasm member THREAD globals MODULE INDEX | table MODULE TABLE ELEMENT [path EDGES...] at MEMBER SOURCE
set wasm member THREAD handle SESSION HANDLE [path EDGES...] at MEMBER SOURCE
set wasip1 arg|arg-insert MODULE INDEX HEX | unset wasip1 arg MODULE INDEX
set wasip1 env MODULE HEXKEY HEXVALUE
WASIp1 mutations may append: if-stop STOP_ID (rejects a different pause)
unset wasip1 env MODULE HEXKEY | set wasip1 rights MODULE FD OLD_BASE OLD_INHERIT NEW_BASE NEW_INHERIT
WASIp1 text uses hex bytes (- means empty), up to 4096 raw bytes; rights accept decimal or 0x hex and may only decrease.
ni [THREAD] | nexti [THREAD] (current genuine native trap/top frame; qualified instructions, same-owner direct branches and typed Wasm calls)
ni proves owned targets or a typed-call continuation before execution; VM/unknown targets and unsupported returns retain the stop. First establish step asm THREAD.
disassemble THREAD STOP_ID COUNT (1..32 instructions; no address or offset input)
disassemble-range THREAD STOP_ID COUNT BYTE_OFFSET INSTRUCTION_OFFSET SYMBOLS (bounded owner; COUNT 1..32, SYMBOLS 0|1)
memory MODULE MEMORY OFFSET LENGTH | replace MODULE FUNCTION GENERATION BODY_FILE | help | quit
catch wasm EVENT MODULE FUNCTION|all | info wasm-events | delete|enable|disable wasm-event ID
trace wasm on [EVENT] | trace wasm off|clear | trace wasm read [AFTER_SEQUENCE [COUNT]] (COUNT=1..128)
wasm-script COMMAND; COMMAND (up to 16 diagnostic/policy commands, including ABI-checked replace; no resume/step or host evaluation)
info registers [REGISTER] | info registers THREAD STOP_ID [REGISTER] (real native trap, top frame only)
ptype NAME | ptype THREAD STOP_ID NAME (scoped C/C++/Rust type layout)
print EXPR | print THREAD STOP_ID EXPR (bounded copied guest selectors, integer/f32/f64 arithmetic, builtin numeric casts and sizeof; no calls)
print-frame THREAD STOP_ID FRAME EXPR | ptype-frame THREAD STOP_ID FRAME EXPR (explicit source frame, any expression prefix)
Rust tuple fields: pair.0 / pair.1; Zig conventional pointer dereference: p.* / p.*.field (owned guest bytes only).
display EXPR | info display | undisplay [ID] | enable|disable|delete display [ID]
Displays: at most32 printable expressions of256 bytes; evaluate source frame0 at each new genuine sole-thread stop. Unavailable values retain the entry; no saved pointer/value is reused.
Wasm EVENT: all|throw|exception|gc|memory|table|atomic|call|reference|simd|control. Events are BEFORE instructions, not committed effects.
Trace holds the newest 512 observations, reports overwritten entries, and never invokes scripts on a guest thread.
wait observes a stop/guest exit for at most two seconds; Ctrl+C separately requests a cooperative pause.
IDs and byte offsets are decimal; offsets are relative to the function expression and must name an emitted safe point.
break-source compares embedded DWARF or source-map paths exactly and opens no source text file.
locals source shows only current cooperative numeric direct-local/constant values; unsupported locations are unavailable.
frames [THREAD STOP_ID [FIRST COUNT]], frame [N|THREAD STOP_ID N], up/down [COUNT|THREAD STOP_ID COUNT] select real source frames.
frames wasm THREAD STOP_ID FIRST COUNT lists canonical Wasm frames without DWARF; pages contain at most128 rows and report the full total.
Caller values require their authenticated saved source PC and typed packet; unavailable locations are reported; resume/replacement/native stepping retire selection.
print/ptype THREAD STOP_ID FRAME NAME and locals source THREAD STOP_ID FRAME query a frame atomically without changing selection.
step wasm (also step THREAD or s THREAD) resumes all participants and stops at the next emitted
Wasm instruction safe point; other participants may advance before parking.
Wasm over skips child/tail-successor activations; out follows this activation through tail calls to its caller or guest exit.
Both use actual Wasm activation identities without DWARF; breakpoints and catchpoints interrupt over/out.
source into/over execute the innermost activation; out follows a selected DWARF frame or the current physical source-map frame. Actual full-JIT activation identities and DWARF scopes or Source Map v3 coordinates are required.
asm executes exactly one native instruction on a qualified LLVM-full JIT thread; other guests stay stopped.
memory reads at most 256 bytes and requires all guest threads stopped.
locals shows up to 256 typed values from the selected stopped thread.
replacement requires an owner-controlled regular body file, exact function ABI, and a stopped guest without an active target frame.
Use tools/debug/secure_server.py for an authorized server launched before guest entry.
Interactive c/continue waits for an actual stop; c&/continue& runs in the background.
Piped/script input keeps asynchronous continue; controller/server/DAP resume is unchanged.
Ctrl+C cancels partial input and requests a cooperative pause; a blocked host timeout keeps its request pending.
Up/Down or Ctrl+P/Ctrl+N recall 32 commands; Ctrl+A/E/B/F, Backspace, Ctrl+U/K/W edit the line.
Ctrl+_ or Ctrl+X Ctrl+U undo current input edits; Alt+F/B move by word and Alt+D/Alt+Backspace kill words.
Ctrl+Y restores killed input text; the command still needs Enter and stays within 8448 input bytes (WASIp1 text4096, legacy grammar512, raw memory256 bytes).
Ctrl+T transposes characters; Ctrl+V quotes printable input (newline/tab become spaces); Ctrl+O accepts and recalls the next history line.
Ctrl/Alt+Left/Right move by word; Alt+< / Alt+> select first history / current draft; Alt+digits repeat bounded input edits.
Bracketed paste treats newlines as spaces and requires Enter after its closing marker; overflow or incomplete markers reject the whole line.
Ctrl+L redraws; Tab completes commands, replace/tui source paths and current source variables/members and break MODULE function symbols; Ctrl+R/S search history backward/forward, Ctrl+G restores the search draft. Alt+Y cycles the immediate prior yank.
Empty Enter repeats eligible step/query commands; replacement/scripts/resume are never implicitly repeated.
s/step, n/next, finish select source into/over/out; si/stepi, bt/where, disas use the sole current stopped thread.
until/u FILE:LINE|LINE | advance/adv FILE:LINE|LINE (sole stopped thread, innermost frame); explicit until/advance THREAD STOP FILE:LINE|LINE.
Exact embedded statement in the origin module; until skips recursive calls, advance may enter them; both stop after return.
Explicit s THREAD/step THREAD retain Wasm stepping. i r, i b, i threads are info aliases.
Ctrl+D deletes under the cursor; on empty input it behaves as EOF.
Unique command prefixes (cont, hel, info reg) and GDB aliases (backtrace, f, d/del) are accepted; ambiguous prefixes are rejected.
LLDB aliases: thread step-in/step-over/step-out/step-inst/step-inst-over, thread backtrace/list, process continue/interrupt/status, frame variable/select, register read, breakpoint list/set/delete.
Breakpoints use explicit Wasm identities: b MODULE FUNCTION OFFSET or b MODULE FILE:LINE; unique published function symbols are supported; arbitrary native addresses and VM/host debugging remain unavailable.
Managed CLI quit requests bounded real cleanup; pending keeps owners and permits status/help/quit retry.
quit force explicitly terminates this process without claiming finalizers. CtrlD may retain a pending prompt.
A standalone launcher may preselect process termination after actual pipe EOF cannot complete cleanup.
Without an installed managed cleanup owner, quit/EOF retains the launcher's process termination policy.
